methods.label: Match each member to a committee pair
methods.explanation:
Each member belongs to exactly two committees, so identify a member by that pair. Name the committees \(A,B,C,D\). Their six unordered pairs are
\[
AB,\ AC,\ AD,\ BC,\ BD,\ CD.
\]
By rule (2), every listed pair has exactly one common member. Different pairs cannot have the same common member: belonging to two different pairs would put that person in at least three committees, contrary to rule (1). Conversely, every club member appears for one listed pair, since each belongs to exactly two committees. Thus there are exactly six distinct members.

This size is attainable: create one member for each listed pair and place that member in precisely those two committees. Both rules then hold. Therefore
\[
x=\boxed{6},
\]
a single value between \(4\) and \(8\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
